leftEvidence.title: A woman anoints Jesus, burial speech answers objection, and Judas agrees on thirty silver pieces

points.label: Gift
points.left: Costly ointment is poured on Jesus’s head.
points.right: Pure nard is poured on Jesus’s head after the jar is broken.

points.label: Objection and memory
points.left: Disciples object, and the act is joined to burial and worldwide telling.
points.right: Some object, and the act is joined to burial and worldwide memory.

points.label: Betrayal arrangement
points.left: Judas asks what he will receive and is weighed thirty silver pieces.
points.right: Judas approaches the priests, who promise money, and seeks an opportunity.

payload.posture: Keep each Scripture witness intact, inspect what each states, and do not supply a combined sequence the sources do not author.

rightEvidence.title: A woman anoints Jesus’s head, burial speech answers indignation, and Judas seeks an opportunity after promised money

payload.tension: The witnesses closely parallel the movement from costly anointing to betrayal while preserving different speakers and transaction details.
payload.title: Anointing and betrayal before the meal
